newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end lower for second day in row.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end lower for second day in row.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed lower for the second successive day on Wednesday as local investors continued to book profits and cut losses, brokers said.
The all share index ended 1.89 points lower at 589.94. Losers outnubmered gainers by 25 to 14.
"Local investors are using recent gains which came after so long to book profit and cut losses," said Dimantha Kohombanwickramage of NDBS Stock Brokers.
The all share index eased for the first time in nearly a month on Tuesday after a slow but steady rise since September 10 when it was 558.10.
"I believe the all share could find support at around the 570 level," said Kohombanwickramage.
Trade volume was an active 2.6 million shares totalling 71 million rupees, supported by foreign buying of Sampath Bank, which traded unchnged at 46.50 rupees.

The stock exchange said today shares in the local subsidiary of oil firm Caltex, Lanka Lubricants, will begin trading next Monday. The company made a public offer of 11.7 million shares at 50 rupees per share in July.
National Development Bank fell 4.75 rupees to 190 and Richard Pieris & Co five to 91. - Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
